parts.final_form: proof: assumption, odd cube shown odd, conclusion
parts.ms: B1 assumption, e.g. n³ even but n odd (contrapositive phrasing condoned); M1 cube an odd number (2p + 1)³; A1 8p³ + 12p² + 6p + 1; A1 reason (2(4p³ + 6p² + 3p) + 1 is odd), contradiction and conclusion. B0M1A1A1 possible (MS pp.7–8)

parts.final_form: A(−4, 0); B shown with evidence for 20

parts.ask: Show the tangent at B is 7y + 4x − 80 = 0
parts.ms: M1 dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt); A1 (3t² − 4)/(4t − 6); M1 t = −2 ⇒ gradient −4/7; M1 line through (20, 0) (if y = mx + c, find c); A1* cso 7y + 4x − 80 = 0 (MS pp.11–12)

parts.ask: The tangent at B meets the curve again at P: find, using algebra, the x coordinate of P
parts.ms: M1 substitute x(t), y(t) into the tangent; A1 7t³ + 8t² − 52t − 80 = 0; dM1 solve for t ≠ −2 ((t + 2)²(7t − 20)) and find x; A1 cso −40/49 (MS pp.11–12)

parts.ask: C: y = x^(sin x), x > 0: by first taking natural logs, find dy/dx in terms of x and y
parts.final_form: dy/dx = y(sin x/x + ln x cos x)
parts.ms: B1 ln y = sin x ln x; M1 ln y → (1/y) dy/dx; M1 product rule on sin x ln x; A1 (1/y)dy/dx = sin x/x + ln x cos x; A1 dy/dx = y sin x/x + y ln x cos x oe (in x only also fine). Alt via e^(sin x ln x) (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: Hence show that x coordinates of stationary points satisfy tan x + x ln x = 0
parts.ms: M1 dy/dx = 0, divide by y to a simplified equation in x; A1* cso via sin x/cos x + x ln x = 0 shown (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ms: M1 separate ∫A^(−3/2) dA = ∫(1/5)t^(−2) dt; M1 one side integrated; M1 both sides; A1 −2A^(−½) = −(1/5)t^(−1) (+c); M1 t = 3, A = 2.25 to find c (= −19/15); M1 rearrange correctly (common denominator, invert both sides, square both sides); A1 cso A = (30t/(19t + 3))² (MS pp.21–22)

parts.ask: l: r = (1, −10, −9) + λ(4, 4, 2); OA is a unit vector parallel to l: find OA
parts.ms: M1 |(4, 4, 2)| = 6 and divide; A1 (2/3)i + (2/3)j + (1/3)k oe in vector form (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: X is the point on l closest to the origin: find the coordinates of X
parts.ms: M1 general point (1 + 4λ, −10 + 4λ, −9 + 2λ); dM1 OX·(4, 4, 2) = 0 (or minimise |OX|²); ddM1 solve for λ; A1 λ = 1.5; A1 (7, −4, −6) (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: Find the exact area of triangle OXA
parts.ms: M1 |OX| = √101 and |OA| = 1; dM1 area = ½|OX| × 1 (right angle at O, since OX ⊥ l and OA ∥ l), or vector-product/scalar-product methods; A1 √101/2 (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: Given y = 1 at x = 0, solve dy/dx = 6xy^(1/3)/e^(2x), y ≥ 0, giving y² = g(x)
parts.ms: B1 separate ∫y^(−1/3) dy = ∫6xe^(−2x) dx; M1 y^(−1/3) → y^(2/3); M1 parts the right way on xe^(−2x); dM1 complete to …xe^(−2x) ± …e^(−2x); A1 (3/2)y^(2/3) = −3xe^(−2x) − (3/2)e^(−2x) + c; M1 (0, 1) gives c = 3; A1 cso y² = (−2xe^(−2x) − e^(−2x) + 2)³ (MS p.16)

parts.ask: Hence find the equation of the horizontal asymptote to y² = g(x)
parts.ms: M1 e^(−2x) → 0 as x → ∞ so y² = 2³; A1 y = 2^(3/2) oe such as √8 (± condoned) (MS p.16)

parts.ask: A, B, C collinear with B between A and C, AB : AC = 1 : 3: show that c = 3b − 2a
parts.ms: M1 two of AB = b − a, AC = c − a, BC = c − b; dM1 use the ratio, e.g. c − b = 2(b − a); A1* c = 3b − 2a with brackets expanded (MS p.17)

parts.ask: For n ∈ ℕ, prove by contradiction that if n² is a multiple of 3 then n is a multiple of 3
parts.final_form: proof: assumption, both non-multiple cases, conclusion
parts.ms: B1 assume n is not a multiple of 3 yet n² is; M1 n = 3p + 1 or 3p + 2 and square one; M1 both; A1 forms showing not multiples of 3, e.g. 3(3p² + 2p) + 1, 3(3p² + 4p + 1) + 1; A1 correct reasons and conclusion (B0M1M1A1A1 possible) (MS pp.17–18)

parts.ask: Curve 2x − 4y² + 3x²y = 4x² + 8 through P(3, 2): find the equation of the normal at P in the form ax + by + c = 0, integers
parts.ms: M1 chain rule y² → …y dy/dx; M1 product rule on 3x²y; A1 2 − 8y dy/dx + 6xy + 3x² dy/dx = 8x; M1 substitute (3, 2) for dy/dx (exactly two dy/dx terms); A1 −14/11; dM1 normal with negative reciprocal through (3, 2); A1 11x − 14y − 5 = 0 or integer multiple, "= 0" seen (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Find the particular solution of dy/dx = 4y²/√(4x + 5), x > −5/4, with y = 1/3 at x = −1/4, as y = f(x)
parts.ms: B1 separate ∫(1/y²) dy = ∫4/√(4x + 5) dx; M1 one side to correct form; A1 −1/y = 2√(4x + 5) (+c); dM1 substitute y = 1/3, x = −1/4 to find c; ddM1 rearrange a/y = b√(4x + 5) + c to y = … correctly (not term-by-term inversion); A1 1/(7 − 2√(4x + 5)) oe; splitting into 1/7 − 1/(2√(4x + 5)) afterwards is A0 (MS p.8)

parts.ask: g(x) = (3x³ + 8x² − 3x − 6)/(x(x + 3)) ≡ Ax + B + C/x + D/(x + 3): find A, B, C, D
parts.ms: M1 correct identity (or divide by x² + 3x for a linear quotient); dM1 method for two constants; A1 two correct; ddM1 method for all four (e.g. compare coefficients); A1 all correct (MS pp.9–10)

parts.ask: For y = g(x), x > 0, use (a) to find g′(x)
parts.ms: M1 C/x + D/(x + 3) → …/x² + …/(x + 3)²; A1ft A − C/x² − D/(x + 3)² with their constants simplified (MS pp.9–10)

parts.ask: Hence explain why g′(x) > 3 for all x in the domain
parts.ms: B1 needs correct (a) and (b): for x > 0, 2/x² > 2/(x + 3)², so 2/x² − 2/(x + 3)² > 0 and g′(x) > 3 (MS pp.9–10)

parts.ms: B1 1 + ½(−4x²); M1 3rd or 4th term structure (condone failing to square/cube the 4); A1 two of −2x², −2x⁴, −4x⁶; A1 all four (list allowed) (MS p.11)

parts.ask: By substituting x = 1/4, obtain an approximation for √3 to 4 d.p.
parts.ms: M1 substitute x = 1/4 into both sides (LHS √3/2) and double; A1 1.7324 cao — the calculator value 1.7321 is not accepted (MS p.11)

parts.ms: M1 dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt); A1 16sec²t tan t/(2sec²t) = 8tan t; dM1 tan t = −1 (t = −π/4); A1 cso −8, not from differentiating the cartesian form (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: C is y = f(x), f quadratic: find f(x) in the form a(x + b)² + c
parts.ms: M1 use 1 + tan²t = sec²t with x and y substituted; A1 1 + (x − 5)²/4 = y/8; A1 y = 2(x − 5)² + 8 (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: Find the range of f
parts.ms: M1 one correct end (strict condoned); A1 8 ≤ f ≤ 32 or [8, 32] (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ms: B1 V = 16πh (dV/dh = 16π); B1 dV/dt = 0.6π − 0.15πh; M1 dV/dt = dV/dh × dh/dt; A1* given result with no errors (unexplained one-liner gets B1B1M1A0) (MS p.19)

parts.ask: Depth 0.5 m when the tap is opened: find the time for the depth to reach 3.5 m
parts.ms: M1 separate and integrate to ±a ln(12 − 3h) = ±bt + c; A1 −(1/3)ln(12 − 3h) = t/320 + c; M1 t = 0, h = 0.5 for c; A1 correct h–t equation; dM1 substitute h = 3.5; A1 207–208 minutes with units (or (320/3)ln 7) (MS pp.19–20)

parts.ask: Complete line 5 of a student's proof by contradiction that if n³ is even then n is even (n = 2p + 1 expanded)
parts.ms: B1 2(4p³ + 6p² + 3p) + 1 with statement that it is odd (even + even + even + 1 = odd accepted) (MS p.21)

parts.ask: Hence prove by contradiction that ∛2 is irrational
parts.final_form: proof: assumption p/q in simplest form, contradiction, conclusion
parts.ms: M1 assume ∛2 = p/q and cube: p³ = 2q³; A1 p³ even so p even; M1 p = 2m ⇒ q³ = 4m³; A1 q³ even so q even; A1* contradiction with simplest form, so ∛2 irrational — "simplest form" must be in the assumption, implications the right way round (MS p.21)

parts.ask: Curve xy² = x²y + 6: find the equation of the tangent at P(2, 3) in the form ax + by + c = 0 with integers a, b, c
parts.final_form: ax + by + c = 0, integers, all terms on one side (3x − 8y + 18 = 0)
parts.ms: M1 implicit differentiation (a k·xy dy/dx or k·x² dy/dx term); dM1 product rule on xy² or x²y; A1 y² + 2xy dy/dx = 2xy + x² dy/dx; M1 substitute (2, 3) and rearrange for dy/dx (= 3/8); dM1 tangent through (2, 3) with their gradient; A1 3x − 8y + 18 = 0 or integer multiple (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Find the first three non-zero terms, in ascending powers of x, of the binomial expansion of ∛(1 + 4x³), |x| < 1/∛4, coefficients as simplified fractions
parts.ms: M1 1 ± (1/3)(4x³…); M1 correct structure of third term (binomial coefficient with (4x³)²); A1 1 + (4/3)x³ or −(16/9)x⁶; A1 1 + (4/3)x³ − (16/9)x⁶ (mixed fractions allowed, not "+−") (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Use the expansion with x = 1/3 to find a rational approximation to ∛31
parts.ms: M1 1 + 4(1/3)³ = 31/27, or substitute x = 1/3 into the expansion; dM1 multiply by 3 (∛27); A1 cao 6869/2187; calculator cube root alone gets nothing (MS p.8)

parts.ask: x = 3 + 2sin t, y = 6/(7 + cos 2t), −π/2 ≤ t ≤ π/2: show C has cartesian equation y = 12/((7 − x)(1 + x)), p ≤ x ≤ q, finding p and q
parts.ms: M1 cos 2t = 1 − 2sin²t to get y in sin t; M1 substitute sin t = (x − 3)/2; A1 correct x–y equation; M1 simplify and factorise the denominator (difference of squares); A1* given result, no errors; B1 p = 1, q = 5 (or 1 ≤ x ≤ 5). Several equivalent routes (MS pp.9–11)

parts.ask: Hence find a cartesian equation in the form y = a/(x + b) + c/(x + d), p ≤ x ≤ q
parts.ms: M1 partial fractions on 12/((7 − x)(1 + x)) finding one constant; A1 one correct term in the required form; A1 3/(2(x + 1)) − 3/(2(x − 7)) oe in the given form (MS pp.10–11)

parts.ask: Expanding regular icosahedron, 20 equilateral faces of side x cm: show its surface area is A = 5√3x²
parts.final_form: given result with one face area shown
parts.ms: M1 surd area of one face, e.g. ½x²sin 60° = (√3/4)x²; A1* 20 × (√3/4)x² = 5√3x², face area shown (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: Given V = (5/12)(3 + √5)x³, show that dV/dA = (3 + √5)x/(8√3)
parts.ms: M1 dA/dx = 10√3x and dV/dx = (15/12)(3 + √5)x²; M1 chain rule dV/dA = (dV/dx) ÷ (dA/dx); A1* given result with dV/dA = … seen (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: Surface area increasing at 0.025 cm² s⁻¹: find the rate of change of volume when x = 2, to 2 s.f.
parts.ms: B1 dA/dt = 0.025; M1 dV/dt = dV/dA × dA/dt at x = 2; A1 awrt 0.019 (units condoned) (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: Curve x = √(9 − 4t), y = t³/√(9 + 4t), 0 ≤ t ≤ 9/4; region R bounded by curve and both axes: show area = K∫₀^(9/4) t³/√(81 − 16t²) dt, finding K
parts.ms: M1 dx/dt = k(9 − 4t)^(−1/2); M1 area = ∫y (dx/dt) dt; ddM1 combine to one fraction with one square root; A1 difference of squares and limits handled (reversal of limits removes the minus sign) to 2∫₀^(9/4)… (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: Using u = 81 − 16t² or otherwise, find the exact area of R (no calculator-only solutions)
parts.ms: B1 du/dt = −32t oe; M1 full substitution into an integral in u only; A1ft multiple of ∫(81u^(−1/2) − u^(1/2)) du; M1 integrate u^(±1/2) terms; ddM1 limits 0 and 81 (or 0 and 9/4 in t); A1 243/64 (−243/64 is A0 unless "area is 243/64" stated). Alts: u² = 81 − 16t², parts (MS pp.14–16)

parts.ask: k, 1 + 2k, 3 + 3k are consecutive terms of a sequence of real numbers: use proof by contradiction to show the sequence is not geometric
parts.ms: B1 assume geometric; M1 equal ratios (1 + 2k)/k = (3 + 3k)/(1 + 2k) to an equation in k; A1 k² + k + 1 = 0; dM1 completing the square/discriminant (−3 < 0) or complex roots to reach a contradiction (no real k); A1 contradiction stated and conclusion (available even if B0) (MS p.17)

parts.ask: Doorknob formed by rotating f(x) = ¼(4 − x)eˣ, 0 ≤ x ≤ 4 (cm), 360° about the x-axis: show V = K∫₀⁴ (x² − 8x + 16)e²ˣ dx, finding K
parts.ms: M1 V = π∫(f(x))² dx (π, limits may be missing); M1 square f(x) with e²ˣ and bracket expanded; A1 (π/16)∫₀⁴(x² − 8x + 16)e²ˣ dx with π, limits and dx (MS pp.18–19)

parts.ask: Hence find the exact volume of the doorknob in the form pπ(e^q + r) cm³, p, q, r simplified rationals
parts.ms: M1 parts the right way: α(x² − 8x + 16)e²ˣ ± β∫(ax − b)e²ˣ dx; A1 correct first application; dM1 parts again and complete; ddM1 apply limits 0, 4 and subtract; A1 (π/64)(e⁸ − 41), π carried from (a) (MS pp.18–20)

parts.ask: A (6, 6, 2), B (6, 0, 7): write down an equation for the line l₁ through A and B in the form r = p + λq
parts.ms: M1 difference of the position vectors (±(0, −6, 5)); A1 e.g. r = (6, 6, 2) + λ(0, −6, 5), "r =" required (MS pp.21–22)

parts.ask: l₂: r = (3, 1, 4) + μ(1, 5, 9): show that l₁ and l₂ do not meet (bold "not")
parts.ms: M1 equate and extract an equation in λ, μ; A1 one correct parameter (μ = 3 from the i-component); M1 substitute into both other equations to compare; A1 values of λ disagree (−5/3 vs 29/5) and conclusion that lines do not meet (MS pp.21–23)

parts.ask: C is on l₂ where μ = −1: find the acute angle between AC and l₂ in degrees to 1 d.p.

parts.ask: Find the derivative with respect to y of 1/(1 + 2ln y)²
parts.ms: M1 form K/(y(1 + 2ln y)³); A1 −4/(y(1 + 2ln y)³) oe (MS pp.24–25)

parts.ask: Hence find a general solution of 3cosec(2x) dy/dx = y(1 + 2ln y)³, y > 0, −π/2 < x < π/2
parts.ms: M1 separate with one side correct and integrated to the right form; M1 both sides; A1 one side integrated correctly; A1 fully correct general solution (constant not required). M1M0A1A0 possible (MS pp.24–25)

parts.ask: Show the particular solution with y = 1 at x = π/6 is y = e^(A sec x − ½), A irrational, finding A
parts.ms: M1 substitute y = 1, x = π/6 to find c; A1 correct equation with c (c = −½ for the 3/(4(1 + 2ln y)²) form); M1 use cos 2x = 2cos²x − 1; ddM1 rearrange, square-root, to ln y = ½((√3/2)sec x − 1); A1 y = e^((√3/4)sec x − ½). No credit for substituting the condition into the given answer (MS pp.24–26)

parts.ask: Find the first 4 terms, ascending powers of x, of the binomial expansion of 2/√(9 − 2x), |x| < 9/2, coefficients as simplified fractions
parts.ms: B1 take out 3: √(9 − 2x) = 3(1 − (2/9)x)^½ (or 2·9^(−½)); M1 3rd/4th term structure of (1 + kx)^(−½); A1 correct (un)simplified expansion; A1 two correct simplified terms; A1 all correct (MS p.8)

parts.ask: By substituting x = 1, find an approximation for √7 to 4 d.p.
parts.ms: M1 substitute x = 1 (LHS 2/√7) and divide into 2 (or equivalent); A1 2.6477. Alternative: multiply by 7/2 giving 2.6438 also credited (MS p.8)

parts.ms: M1 x = 4 in C gives 3-term quadratic in y; M1 solve; A1 y = −10 (reject 2); M1 substitute (4, −10) into dy/dx; A1 −9/2 (MS p.10)

parts.ms: B1 separate ∫dV/(300 − kV) = ∫dt; M1 → α ln(300 − kV); A1 −(1/k)ln(300 − kV) = t + c; M1 remove the ln correctly; A1* V = 300/k + Ae^(−kt) (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Initially empty; at t = 10 volume increasing at 200 cm³ s⁻¹: find the exact value of k
parts.ms: M1 V = 0 at t = 0 gives A = −300/k; M1 dV/dt = 300e^(−kt) (or use dV/dt = 300 − kV ⇒ kV = 100); M1 e^(−10k) = 2/3 ⇒ k; A1 k = (1/10)ln(3/2) oe (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Hence find the time for the volume to reach 6 litres, to the nearest second
parts.ms: M1 set V = 6000 and solve for t; A1 t = 41 (MS p.14)

parts.final_form: given integral with α = 0, β = π
parts.ms: M1 V = π∫y²(dx/dθ) dθ; M1 sin 2θ = 2sin θ cos θ; A1 correct integral in sin θ, cos θ; A1* correct limits (reversal removes the minus), π present throughout (MS p.16)

parts.ask: Use u = cos θ and algebraic integration to show V = kπ, k rational
parts.ms: M1 substitute correctly (dθ = du/(−sin θ)); M1 change limits to u = ±1; A1 −5π∫(1 − u²)(3 − 2u)² du in u only; M1 expand; A1 9 − 12u − 5u² + 12u³ − 4u⁴; M1 integrate and apply u limits; A1 cao 196π/3 (MS p.16)

parts.ms: B1 A = 1/9 (parts (a) and (b) marked as a whole) (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Given C = 3B, show that k² + 6k = 0
parts.ms: B1 correct unsimplified x and x² coefficients, e.g. B = −2k/27, C = k²/27 (3^(−2) may be missing); M1 set their C = 3 × their B to get a two-term quadratic in k; A1* given answer from a correct equation (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Hence find the value of k
parts.ms: B1 k = −6 only; k = 0 must be rejected (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Find the value of D
parts.ms: M1 substitute their non-zero k into a correct x³ coefficient including 3^(−2); A1 32/9 oe (MS p.7)

parts.ms: B1 identity 1 ≡ A(1 − x) + B(1 + 3x); M1 find one constant; A1 3/(4(1 + 3x)) + 1/(4(1 − x)) (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Hence solve (1 + 3x)(1 − x) dy/dx = tan y, −1/3 < x ≤ 1/2, with y = π/2 at x = 1/2; give the answer as sinⁿy = f(x), n an integer to be found

parts.ms: B1 dA/dt = −0.5; B1 A = πx², dA/dx = 2πx; M1 chain rule dx/dt = (dA/dt)/(dA/dx); A1cso awrt −0.0114 or −1/(28π), negative sign required (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Find, according to the model, the rate of decrease of the volume when x = 4
parts.ms: B1 V = πx²(3x) = 3πx³; B1ft dV/dx = 9πx²; M1 dV/dx × dx/dt with dx/dt in terms of x (not the (a) value); A1 9 (sign optional) (MS p.9)

parts.ms: B1 8y³ → 24y² dy/dx; M1 product rule on −9kx²y → …kxy … − 9kx² dy/dx; M1 collect dy/dx terms, factorise, divide; A1* no errors (MS pp.10–11)

parts.ask: Given a turning point at x = 5/2, find the value of k
parts.ms: M1 dy/dx = 0 with x = 5/2 (numerator) or substitute x = 5/2 in the curve; A1 15ky − 100 = 0 or 250 − (225/4)ky + 8y³ = 875; M1 solve simultaneously for k (y = 5); A1 k = 4/3 (MS pp.10–11)

parts.ask: All stages shown, no calculator: use x = 2sin u to show that ∫₀¹ (3x + 2)/(4 − x²)^(3/2) dx = ∫₀^p ((3/2)sec u tan u + ½sec²u) du, finding p
parts.ms: B1 p = π/6 (30 is B0); M1 dx/du = 2cos u; M1 full substitution using sin²u + cos²u = 1 in the denominator; A1* given answer with du and an intermediate step simplifying the power (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Hence find the exact value of ∫₀¹ (3x + 2)/(4 − x²)^(3/2) dx
parts.ms: M1 integrate to …sec u + …tan u; A1 (3/2)sec u + ½tan u; M1 substitute p and 0 and subtract; A1 7√3/6 − 3/2 oe (MS p.12)

parts.ms: M1 AB = 4i + 7j − 5k (either way); M1 OA or OB + λ(their AB); A1 correct equation with r = (l = is A0) (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Given AC is perpendicular to l, find p
parts.ms: M1 AC = 2i + (p + 4)j − 4k; M1 scalar product of AB and AC = 0, solve linear equation; A1 p = −8 (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Hence find the area of triangle ABC as a surd in simplest form
parts.ms: M1 |AB| = √90 or |AC| = 6; dM1 area = ½|AB||AC| (or other complete exact method); A1 9√10 (MS p.13)

parts.ask: All stages shown, no calculator: C: x = sin t − 3cos²t, y = 3sin t + 2cos t, 0 ≤ t ≤ 5; show dy/dx = 3 where t = π
parts.ms: B1 dx/dt = cos t + 6cos t sin t; B1 dy/dt = 3cos t − 2sin t; M1 divide and substitute t = π; A1* = 3 with full working (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Find the equation of the tangent at P (t = π) in the form y = mx + c
parts.ms: B1 x = −3, y = −2; M1 tangent with gradient 3 (if y = mx + c used, find c); A1 y = 3x + 7 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: The tangent cuts C again at Q: show that t at Q satisfies 9cos²t + 2cos t − 7 = 0
parts.ms: M1 substitute the parametric equations into their tangent; A1* given equation, no errors (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Hence find the exact y coordinate of Q
parts.ms: B1 cos t = 7/9; M1 evaluate y = 3sin t + 2cos t (awrt 3.44 implies); A1 4√2/3 + 14/9 oe — withheld if extra answers given (MS p.14)

parts.ms: M1 correct unsimplified π∫(10xe^(−x/2))² dx; A1 100π∫₀¹⁰ x²e^(−x) dx (limits required) (MS p.15)

parts.ask: Find ∫x²e^(−x) dx
parts.ms: M1 parts in the right direction: …x²e^(−x) ± …∫xe^(−x) dx; dM1 parts again; A1 −x²e^(−x) − 2xe^(−x) − 2e^(−x) (+c optional); tabular method accepted (MS p.15)

parts.ask: Exercise weight = two such solids joined (20 cm long, mass 5 kg): using (a) and (b), find its density in g/cm³ to 3 s.f.
parts.final_form: 3 s.f. in g/cm³: awrt 3.99 (MS prints the unit in brackets, so it is not required; exact 25/(π(2 − 122e^(−10))) oe accepted)
parts.ms: M1 total volume = 2 × 100π × ∫₀¹⁰ x²e^(−x) dx; M1 limits 10 and 0 in (b) (limits 20 and 0 also allowed); A1 2 − 122e^(−10) (≈ 1.994); dM1 density = 5000/their volume (grams); A1 awrt 3.99 (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: Use proof by contradiction to show that n² − 2 is never divisible by 4 for integer n
parts.ms: M1 algebraic statement engaging with divisibility by 4, e.g. n² − 2 = 4k; A1 n² = 2(2k + 1); dM1 complete argument to a contradiction (n² even ⇒ n even ⇒ n² multiple of 4 ⇒ n² − 2 not); A1* contradiction drawn and conclusion, with an assumption stated at the start. Alts: odd/even cases n = 2m, 2m + 1 giving non-integers or 4 | 2 contradictions (MS pp.16–18)

parts.ask: Curve x = t/(t − 3), y = 1/t + 2, t > 3: show all points lie on y = (ax − 1)/(bx) and find the constants a, b
parts.ms: M1 attempt t (or 1/t) in terms of x or y, e.g. t = 3x/(x − 1); dM1 form cartesian equation and make progress towards y as subject; A1 y = (7x − 1)/(3x) — not just correct a and b. Alt: substitute both into y = (ax − 1)/(bx) and compare coefficients (MS p.7)
parts.er: Good opener, many full marks; most made t the subject from x and substituted into y; a disappointing number stopped at t = x(t − 3) and ended with y in x and t; many could not rearrange to make y the subject; a few used calculus and scored 0 (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Express 3x/((2x − 1)(x − 2)) in partial fractions
parts.ms: M1 correct PF form leading to A, B; A1 one of A = −1, B = 2; A1 −1/(2x − 1) + 2/(x − 2) (may be awarded from work in (b)) (MS p.8)
parts.er: Almost always correct; occasional arithmetic slips or wrong identity (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Hence show that the integral of 3x/((2x − 1)(x − 2)) from 5 to 25 equals ln k, k a fully simplified fraction (no calculator-only solutions)
parts.ms: M1 ∫ → C ln(2x − 1) + D ln(x − 2); A1ft −½ln(2x − 1) + 2ln(x − 2) (brackets needed, may be implied); dM1 substitute 5 and 25 and subtract; A1 cso ln(529/21) (mixed number ln 25 4/21 allowed) (MS p.8)
parts.er: Most integrated 1/(x − 2) correctly but a common error was omitting the ½ in ∫1/(2x − 1) dx = ½ln(2x − 1); log laws well known (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Triangle PQR with PQ = 2i − 3j + 4k, PR = 8i − 5j + 3k: find the vector RQ
parts.ms: M1 subtract PQ and PR either way (PR − QP is M0); A1 RQ = −6i + 2j + k oe, coordinates not accepted (MS p.9)
parts.er: Mostly found; some added the vectors (or changed a sign before subtracting) for no credit; some gave QR (wrong direction) and kept only M1 (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Find the size of angle PQR in degrees to 3 s.f.
parts.ms: M1 scalar product of PQ and their RQ (not PQ·PR); dM1 full attempt at cos PQR = a.b/(|a||b|) with both moduli (one correct); A1 awrt 114 (isw); must come from correct vectors — wrong RQ (e.g. 6i − 2j + k) gives A0 even if 114 stated. Alt: three lengths + cosine rule (MS p.9)
parts.er: Many full marks via scalar product; errors: wrong pair of vectors, or directions giving the acute angle (some then subtracted from 180°); cosine-rule users almost all successful (ER p.3)

parts.ask: g(x) = 1/√(4 − x²): find the first four non-zero terms of the binomial expansion in ascending powers of x, coefficients in simplest form
parts.ms: B1 constant/factor 4^(−1/2) = ½ (was M1 on ePEN); M1 correct binomial coefficient with correct power for the 3rd or 4th term of (1 + ax²)^(−1/2); A1 correct unsimplified; A1 two correct simplified terms; A1 all four (list accepted, ignore higher terms). Alts: direct expansion of (4 − x²)^(−1/2); (2 − x)^(−1/2)(2 + x)^(−1/2) (MS pp.10–11)
parts.er: Expansion in x² caused fewer problems than the previous year; errors: 4 or 4^½ taken out, not dividing x² by 4, not multiplying by the ½, and most commonly sign slips giving alternating signs (ER p.4)

parts.ask: State the range of values of x for which the expansion is valid
parts.ms: B1 |x| < 2 or −2 < x < 2 oe (MS p.10)
parts.er: Many wrong: |x| < 4, x < 2, |x| < ±2 (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Use the expansion from (a) to find a fully simplified rational approximation for √3, showing working
parts.ms: M1 substitute an exact x into both sides allowing √3 to be found (x = 1 or −1 simplest; x = √(8/3), √(11/3) also possible); A1 √3 = 2048/1181 or 3543/2048, only from a correct expansion (MS pp.10–11)
parts.er: x = 1 the most common successful strategy; some set 1/√(4 − x²) = √3 and substituted x = √(11/3) but seldom finished; some substituted x = √3; many gave a rounded decimal, ignoring "rational" (ER p.4)

parts.ask: All stages shown, no calculator-only solutions: region under y = 12√x/(2x² + 3)^1.5 between x = 1/√2 and x = k rotated 360° about the x-axis has volume 713π/648; use algebraic integration to find the exact value of k
parts.ms: B1 V = π∫ y² dx with limits 1/√2, k and π (limits may appear later); M1 ∫ 144x/(2x² + 3)³ dx → A(2x² + 3)^(−2) (or Au^(−2) with u = 2x² + 3); A1 −18(2x² + 3)^(−2); M1 apply limits to an attempt at ∫y² (not y) and set equal to 713/648; ddM1 solve to (2k² + 3)² = 729 or a quadratic in k² and find k; A1 k = 2√3 (MS p.12)
parts.er: Done well only by the most able; first B1 often lost by not squaring y or dropping π; main stumbling block was choosing a method: few recognised a reverse chain rule of (2x² + 3)^(−2) or u = 2x² + 3; wasted time on parts, ln(2x² + 3)³, wrong division; even correct integrators struggled with the algebra for k (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Curve x = 1 + 3tan t, y = 2cos 2t, −π/6 ≤ t ≤ π/3, crosses the x-axis at P: find the equation of the tangent at P in the form y = mx + c
parts.ms: B1 t = π/4 or x = 4 at P; M1 dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt); A1 −4sin 2t/(3sec²t) oe; dM1 tangent at t = π/4 through (4, 0); A1 y = −(2/3)x + 8/3 (MS p.13)
parts.er: Standard bookwork, most worked in radians and found t = π/4; errors: wrong derivative, simplifying 1/(3sec²t) to 3cos²t, using x = π/4 in the tangent equation (ER p.5)

parts.ask: C is y = f(x) with domain [k, 1 + 3√3]: find the exact value of k
parts.er: Most who answered substituted t = −π/6 correctly, but the part was often left blank (ER p.5) [the ER prints t = π/4 here, apparently a slip: k = 1 + 3tan(−π/6) = 1 − √3 uses the lower parameter limit t = −π/6]

parts.ask: Find the range of f
parts.ms: M1 either end correct (strict allowed; f < 2 scores, f > 2 does not); A1 −1 ≤ f ≤ 2 oe, e.g. [−1, 2] or −1 ≤ y ≤ 2 (MS p.13)
parts.er: Only abler candidates got both marks; lower bound (t = π/3) found more often than the upper; many missed that the maximum is at t = 0 and used t = π/3, giving −1 ≤ f ≤ 1 (ER p.5)

parts.ask: All stages shown, no calculator-only solutions: use u = eˣ − 3 to show that the integral of 4e³ˣ/(eˣ − 3) from ln 5 to ln 7 equals a + b ln 2, finding a and b
parts.ms: B1 du/dx = eˣ (or dx/du = 1/(u + 3)); M1 integrand fully in u, P(u + 3)³/(u(u + 3)) form, du not dx; A1 4(u + 3)²/u du; dM1 expand and integrate, one term P ln u; A1 2u² + 24u + 36 ln u; M1 limits u = 2 and 4 (or back-substitute and use x limits); A1 72 + 36 ln 2. The 4 must be present for A marks (MS pp.14–15)
parts.er: B1 usually scored; weaker candidates could not write the integrand in u; losses: dropping the 4, integrating by parts instead of expanding, using the x limits ln 7 and ln 5 instead of 4 and 2 (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Show by integration that ∫3eˣcos 2x dx = peˣsin 2x + qeˣcos 2x + c, finding p and q
parts.ms: M1 parts once: Aeˣsin 2x ± B∫eˣsin 2x dx; A1 (3/2)eˣsin 2x − (3/2)∫eˣsin 2x dx; dM1 parts again giving ± C∫eˣcos 2x dx; ddM1 collect the two ∫eˣcos 2x dx terms; A1 (6/5)eˣsin 2x + (3/5)eˣcos 2x + c. Either choice of u accepted (MS pp.14–15)
parts.er: Often not attempted; most who tried knew parts; common errors integrating/differentiating cos 2x, signs and constants; many lost the final A1; some forgot the factor 3; fully correct answers not common (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Complete a student's proof by contradiction that no positive integers x, y satisfy 3x² + 2xy − y² = 25 (start given: (3x − y)(x + y) = 25, case 1 and 25 shown non-integer)
parts.final_form: remaining cases solved + reason ("not integers") + concluding statement
parts.ms: M1 solve one other case (3x − y = 25, x + y = 1 or both = 5); A1 one solved correctly (x = 6.5, y = −5.5 or x = y = 2.5); dM1 both cases; A1 both correct, reason for contradiction and conclusion (e.g. "hence proven"); negative-factor cases may be ignored; final A withheld if cases not giving 25 are included (MS p.16)
parts.er: Many did not attempt or just rewrote the given proof; most considered only one case (both = 5 more often than 25 and 1); 3x − y = 25, x + y = 1 often wrongly given y = 18.5 by copying; few lacked a conclusion (ER p.6)

parts.ask: l₁: r = (2, 8, 10) + λ(−1, 2, 3), l₂: r = (−4, −1, 2) + μ(5, 4, 8): prove the lines are skew
parts.final_form: proof: no intersection (shown by inconsistency) AND not parallel, with conclusion
parts.ms: M1 solve two of the three component equations for λ and μ; A1 correct values (e.g. λ = −3/2, μ = 3/2 from (1),(2)); dM1 substitute into the third; A1 inconsistency shown plus statement that lines do not intersect ("skew" alone not enough here); A1* cso direction vectors not parallel with minimal reason (e.g. 5 = −5×−1 but 4 ≠ −5×2), then skew. "(5,4,8) ≠ (−1,2,3)" is not a reason (MS pp.17–18)
parts.er: Well prepared; many failed to state that conflicting values mean the lines do not intersect; jumping straight to "skew" showed lack of understanding; many ignored the parallel check, some only wrote the vectors are unequal; a few tested perpendicularity instead (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Melting ice ball, radius 12 cm at t = 0; rate of decrease of r inversely proportional to r²; r = 6 at t = 15 min: find an equation linking r and t
parts.final_form: equation in r and t, e.g. r³ = 1728 − 100.8t (⅓r³ = −33.6t + 576)
parts.ms: B1 dr/dt = −k/r² (or ±k/r²); M1 separate and integrate to αr³ = ±kt + c; A1 ⅓r³ = −kt + c with two different constants; M1 use t = 0, r = 12 and t = 15, r = 6 to find c and k; A1 r³ = −100.8t + 1728 oe. Alt via V = (4/3)πr³ and dV/dt constant (MS pp.19–20)
parts.er: Many could not start: could not write the DE; many omitted the proportionality constant k (max 2 marks); others wrote dr/dt = kr², k√r, k/√r; some did not integrate, forgot + c, or substituted conditions before integrating (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Find the time taken for the ball to melt completely
parts.ms: M1 set r = 0 in their equation (ft); A1 awrt 17.1 minutes with units (17 min 8 or 9 s allowed) (MS pp.19–20)
parts.er: Those attempting it usually set r = 0; units were required for both marks (in context) (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Sketch a graph of r against t on the diagram given
parts.final_form: curve in quadrant 1 from (0, 12), decreasing and getting steeper, to the t-axis
parts.ms: B1 correct shape only in quadrant 1 from (0, 12), gradient increasingly steep (dr/dt = −k/r²) (MS p.20)
parts.er: Correct graphs rare, often left blank; common wrong shapes: straight line or concave curve (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Closed curve (x + y)³ + 10y² = 108x: show that dy/dx = (108 − 3(x + y)²)/(20y + 3(x + y)²)
parts.ms: B1 10y² → 20y dy/dx; M1 (x + y)³ → k(x + y)²(1 + dy/dx) (or expand and differentiate term by term); A1 correct differentiated equation; dM1 collect dy/dx terms; A1* given answer. Working backwards from the answer scores only B1 (MS pp.21–22)
parts.er: "Show that" written to give access to (b): all steps must be seen; differentiation of (x + y)³ needed either chain rule 3(x + y)²(1 + dy/dx) or expansion and product rule clearly applied (ER p.7)

parts.ask: Curve models a cycle track (km); P and Q are the furthest north and south points: using (a), find how far Q is south of O, to the nearest 100 m
parts.final_form: distance to nearest 100 m with units (13 900 m / 13.9 km)
parts.ms: M1 numerator = 0 ⇒ (x + y)² = 36; dM1 substitute x + y = 6 into the curve to get an equation in y (or x); ddM1 solve 216 + 10y² = 108(6 − y) and take the negative root; A1 awrt 13 900 m or 13.9 km with units (−13.9 km condoned) (MS pp.21–22)
parts.er: Many deduced numerator = 0 and (x + y)² = 36; only the very best solved simultaneously to a fully correct answer (ER p.7)

parts.ask: f(x) = (5x + 10)/((1 - x)(2 + 3x)) in partial fractions.
parts.ms: M1 method for A or B; A1 A = 3 or B = 4; A1 3/(1 - x) + 4/(2 + 3x).
parts.er: Accessible; occasional arithmetic or sign slips (ER pp.3-4).

parts.ask: Binomial expansion of f(x) in ascending powers of x up to x^2, coefficients as simplified fractions.
parts.er: The factor 2^-1 mishandled (2 outside the bracket, or ignored), x^2 coefficient errors, sign slips when combining; a few forgot to use (a) (ER pp.3-4).

parts.ask: Range of values of x for which the expansion is valid.
parts.er: An early discriminator: both intervals stated without choosing the narrower one, or |x| < 1, or incompatible inequalities; the reason the modal score was 8/9 (ER pp.3-4).

parts.ask: x = (t - 1)/(2t + 1), y = 6/(2t + 1), t != -1/2: show all points lie on a straight line.
parts.ms: M1 t in terms of x or y (t = (x + 1)/(1 - 2x)); A1 substitute; dM1 simplify to y = ax + b; A1* y = 2(1 - 2x), so linear (conclusion required).
parts.er: Most common loss: no concluding statement that the equation is linear; sign errors rearranging for t; parametric differentiation route rarer (ER pp.4-5).

parts.ask: Hence or otherwise, x coordinate of the intersection with y = x + 12.
parts.ms: M1 solve 2(1 - 2x) = x + 12; A1cao x = -2. Alt: t = -1/5 from the parametric equations, then x.
parts.er: Better done than (a), often via t = -1/5; a few found t but not x (ER pp.4-5).

parts.ask: Complete a student's proof by contradiction that if p^3 is a multiple of 3 then p is (start: p = 3k + 1 case shown).
parts.ms: M1 p = 3k + 2: (3k + 2)^3 = 27k^3 + 54k^2 + 36k + 8; A1 = 3(9k^3 + 18k^2 + 12k + 3) - 1, not a multiple of 3; A1 so p is neither 3k + 1 nor 3k + 2, contradiction, hence p is a multiple of 3.
parts.er: Over 40% scored 0; many repeated the 3k + 1 case or wrote a conclusion without the second case; the final mark needed both cases tied into the contradiction (ER pp.9-11).

parts.ask: Hence prove by contradiction that the cube root of 3 is irrational.
parts.ms: B1 assume cube root 3 = p/q with no common factors; M1 p^3 = 3q^3; A1 so p^3 and hence p (by (a)) is a multiple of 3; dM1 p = 3k gives q^3 = 9k^3; A1* q is a multiple of 3, contradicting no common factors, so irrational.
parts.er: The sqrt2 proof was known but rarely adapted: p a multiple of 3 claimed without p^3, oddness arguments, contradiction claimed too early, and lowest terms not stated (ER pp.9-11).

parts.ask: P(2i - 2j + k); C on l with PC perpendicular to l: coordinates of C.

parts.ask: The integral of x^2 e^x dx.
parts.ms: M1A1 x^2 e^x - integral of 2x e^x dx; M1 parts again; A1 x^2 e^x - 2x e^x + 2e^x (+c).
parts.er: Well known; a sign error in the second application was common (ER p.6).

parts.ask: Substitution u = sqrt(1 - 3x): integral of 27x/sqrt(1 - 3x) dx = -2(1 - 3x)^(1/2)(Ax + B) + k, integers A, B.
parts.ms: B1 2u du/dx = -3 oe; M1 full substitution; A1 6 integral of (u^2 - 1) du oe; A1ft 6(u^3/3 - u); M1 back to x and factorise; A1 -2(1 - 3x)^(1/2)(3x + 2) + k.
parts.er: Errors: differentiating u = (1 - 3x)^(1/2), not converting every part (including dx) to u, and taking out the common factor of (1 - 3x)^(1/2) (ER p.6).

parts.ask: Banner: show all stages of working; solutions relying entirely on calculator technology not acceptable. Engine temperature: d(theta)/dt = -k(theta - 15)^2; theta = 85 at t = 0 and 40 at t = 10: solve to show theta = (at + b)/(ct + d), integers a, b, c, d.
parts.ms: B1 separate; M1A1 -1/(theta - 15) = -kt + c; M1 c = -1/70; M1 k = 9/3500; M1 rearrange for theta; A1 (135t + 4250)/(9t + 50).
parts.er: Very demanding (two constants); omitting the constant of integration was a critical error with no recovery; inverting term by term rarer this series (ER p.6).

parts.ask: Time for the temperature to reach 20 degrees C.
parts.er: Most with (a) scored at least 1; the reciprocal form 1/(theta - 15) = 9t/3500 + 1/70 is a better route (ER p.6).

parts.ask: Proof by contradiction: sqrt7 is irrational (given: if k^2 is a multiple of 7, so is k).
parts.ms: M1 assume sqrt7 = a/b in lowest terms (no common factors) and square; A1 7b^2 = a^2 so a^2 and hence a is a multiple of 7; M1 a = 7k gives b^2 = 7k^2; A1 so b is a multiple of 7, contradicting no common factors; sqrt7 irrational.
parts.er: More familiar than past proofs; omissions: a^2 not mentioned before a, a = 7k not used, the 'no common factors' condition missing from the contradiction (ER p.7).

parts.er: Most achieved (ER pp.7-8).

parts.ask: P at t = 2: coordinates of P.
parts.er: Most achieved (ER pp.7-8).

parts.ask: Using calculus, the normal l at P is 3x + 5y = 15.
parts.er: Surprising errors differentiating t + 1/t and t - 1/t; a minority found the tangent (ER pp.7-8).

parts.ask: R between C, l and the x-axis rotated 2pi about the x-axis: exact volume by algebraic integration.
parts.ms: B1 l meets the x-axis at x = 5; M1 cone (1/3)pi(1.5^2)(2.5) = 15pi/8; M1 V = pi integral of y^2 (dx/dt) dt; M1 expand (t - 1/t)^2(1 - 1/t^2); A1 t^3/3 - 3/t + 1/(3t^3) - 3t; M1 limits 1 and 2; A1 13pi/24 + 15pi/8 = 29pi/12 cao.
parts.er: Discriminating: errors were omitting one of the two volumes, (t - 1/t)^2 = t^2 - 1/t^2, leaving out dx/dt, and using x limits in a t integral (ER pp.7-8).

parts.ask: First four terms of the binomial expansion of 8/(2 - 5x)^2, simplest form.
parts.ms: B1 (2 - 5x)^-2 = (1/4)(1 - 5x/2)^-2; M1A1 binomial with index -2 and -5x/2; A1 2 + 10x + (75/2)x^2 + 125x^3. Direct expansion also accepted.
parts.er: Generally well answered; marks lost by mishandling 2^-2 (giving 2(1 + ...) or 16(1 + ...)), using x or -5x for -5x/2, and sign slips (ER p.3).

parts.ask: Range of x for which the expansion is valid.
parts.er: Poorly answered; wrong answers included x < 2/5, |x| < 5/2, |x| > 2/5 and -1/5 < x < 1/5 (ER p.3).

parts.ask: Cube edge x cm, surface area S cm^2 increasing at 4 cm^2 s^-1, volume V: show dx/dt = k/x and find k.
parts.ms: B1 S = 6x^2 or dS/dt = 4; B1 both; M1 chain rule dS/dt = (dS/dx)(dx/dt); A1 dx/dt = 1/(3x).
parts.er: Most had a suitable approach; common error S = x^2 (also 4x^2, 8x^2) (ER pp.3-4).

parts.ask: dV/dt = V^p; find p.
parts.ms: B1 dV/dx = 3x^2; M1 dV/dt = 3x^2 x 1/(3x) = x; A1 dV/dt = V^(1/3).
parts.er: Usually correct method; errors followed from a wrong S; a surprising number stopped at dV/dt = x (ER pp.3-4).

parts.ask: Banner: show all stages of working; solutions based on calculator technology not acceptable. Integration by parts: exact value of the integral from 0 to 4 of x^2 e^(2x) dx, simplest form.
parts.ms: M1 parts once: (1/2)x^2 e^(2x) - integral of x e^(2x) dx; M1 parts again; A1 (1/2)x^2 e^(2x) - (1/2)x e^(2x) + (1/4)e^(2x); M1 both limits; A1 25e^8/4 - 1/4 (no '+c').
parts.er: Well answered; some ignored the limits (max 3/5), integrated the wrong way round, or took e^0 = 0; a few gave decimals (ER p.4).

parts.ask: Integration by substitution: integral from 3 to 21/2 of 4x/(2x - 1)^2 dx = a + ln b; find a and b.
parts.ms: B1 du = 2dx (u = 2x - 1; u = (2x - 1)^2 or u = 2x also allowed); M1A1 integrand in u, e.g. (u + 1)/u^2; dM1A1 ln u - 1/u; M1 limits 5 and 20; A1 3/20 + ln 4.
parts.er: Mostly u = 2x - 1 and well done; candidates who ignored 'substitution' and used parts or partial fractions could score at most 4/7; x-limits sometimes used in the u-expression (ER p.4).

parts.ask: Proof by contradiction: k + 9/k >= 6 for all positive k.
parts.ms: B1 assume there is a positive k with k + 9/k < 6; M1 multiply by k to k^2 - 6k + 9 < 0 (or other routes); A1 (k - 3)^2 < 0; A1* squares are >= 0, contradiction, so k + 9/k >= 6.
parts.er: Most challenging question: many began with a wrong assumption (e.g. for negative k, or 'for all k'), tested values, or argued algebraically without a contradiction; discriminant users rarely explained; imprecise final reasoning (ER pp.4-5).

parts.ask: Show the result is not true for all real numbers.
parts.ms: B1 e.g. k = -3 gives -6, not >= 6 (or any k < 0 argued generally).
parts.er: Many attempted another proof instead of a counter-example; k = 0 a common wrong choice (ER pp.4-5).

parts.ask: Curve y^3 - x^2 + 4x^2 y = k, k > 1: dy/dx in terms of x and y.
parts.ms: M1 y^3 -> 3y^2 dy/dx; M1 product rule on 4x^2 y; A1 3y^2 dy/dx - 2x + 8xy + 4x^2 dy/dx = 0; M1 collect; A1 dy/dx = (2x - 8xy)/(3y^2 + 4x^2).
parts.er: Done well; slips with coefficients, k differentiated by some, 8xy not treated as a product (ER p.5).

parts.ask: The normal to C at P is y = x: find k.
parts.ms: M1 dy/dx = -1 at P; M1A1 use y = x to get -1 = (2p - 8p^2)/(3p^2 + 4p^2), p = 2; ddM1 substitute into C; A1 k = 36.
parts.er: Less confident: many set the derivative to 0, or used -1 without using y = x to fix the point (ER p.5).

parts.er: Surprising number gave (0, 0, 0) or solved equations at length instead of stating the common point (ER p.6).

parts.ask: Angle theta between l1 and l2: cos(theta) as a fully simplified fraction.
parts.er: Mostly correct with the direction vectors; a few used position vectors or did not simplify (ER p.6).

parts.er: Errors: |OQ| used for PQ, missing 1/2, RQ used as the second side, cos instead of sin; finding Q first was inefficient (ER p.6).

parts.ask: Possible coordinates of R.
parts.er: Sketches helped; a common error was equating the vectors PQ and PR componentwise (ER p.6).

parts.ask: Goats: first model x = k(9t + 5)/(4t + 3) (x in thousands), 3000 goats at t = 0: show k = 1.8.
parts.er: Mostly correct; some used x = 3000 to get 1800 and then divided by 1000, losing a mark (ER pp.6-7).

parts.ask: Long-term population predicted by the first model.
parts.er: Many gave 4.05 without relating it to thousands (4050) (ER pp.6-7).

parts.ask: 3/(x(9 - 2x)) in partial fractions.
parts.er: Usually all 3 marks (ER pp.6-7).

parts.ask: Second model: 3 dx/dt = x(9 - 2x); solve with the initial condition to show x = 9/(2 + e^(-3t)).
parts.ms: M1A1ft separate and integrate: (1/3) ln x - (1/3) ln(9 - 2x) = t (+c); M1 t = 0, x = 3 gives c = 0; ddM1 remove logs; A1* x = 9/(2 + e^(-3t)).
parts.er: Weaker candidates could not apply (c); the main problem was omitting the constant of integration, which blocked further marks (ER pp.6-7).

parts.ask: Long-term population predicted by the second model.
parts.er: Often 4.5 given without context (4500) (ER pp.6-7).

parts.ask: x = 6t - 3 sin 2t, y = 2 cos t, 0 <= t <= pi/2; C meets the x-axis at k: state k.
parts.ms: B1 3pi.
parts.er: Mostly 3pi; some left blank (time pressure noted) (ER pp.7-9).

parts.ask: Parametric differentiation: dy/dx = lambda cosec t; find lambda.
parts.ms: M1A1 dy/dx = -2 sin t/(6 - 6 cos 2t); M1A1* cos 2t = 1 - 2 sin^2 t gives -(1/6) cosec t.
parts.er: Process known; errors in dx/dt and a missing 2 in cos 2t = 1 - 2 sin^2 t (ER pp.7-9).

parts.ask: P at t = pi/4; the tangent at P meets the y-axis at N: exact y coordinate of N.
parts.ms: B1 P(3pi/2 - 3, sqrt2); M1 tangent with gradient -sqrt2/6 and x = 0; A1 pi sqrt2/4 + sqrt2/2 oe.
parts.er: Many omitted it or gave sqrt2 (P's y); inexact P values and algebra slips lost marks (ER pp.7-9).

parts.ask: Region between C and the axes rotated 2pi about the x-axis: (i) show V = integral from 0 to alpha of beta(1 - cos 4t) dt; (ii) hence exact volume.
parts.ms: M1A1 pi y^2 dx/dt = 4 cos^2 t(6 - 6 cos 2t) (times pi); dM1 double angle to 6(1 - cos 4t); A1 V = integral from 0 to pi/2 of 6pi(1 - cos 4t) dt; M1A1 [6pi t - (6pi/4) sin 4t] = 3pi^2.
parts.er: (d)(i) among the hardest items: many got y^2 dx/dt then could not reach the required integrand; dx/dt omitted, wrong upper limit (3pi) or pi lost; (ii) often not attempted although its method mark was available (ER pp.7-9).

parts.er: Accessible, most full marks; errors: x or 4x used instead of -4x, constant term omitted; writing 1/(1 - 4x)^3 and expanding the denominator scored 0 (ER p.3).

parts.ms: M1 identity 3x + 4 = A(2x + 1)^2 + B(x - 2)(2x + 1) + C(x - 2) and a method; A1 one correct; M1 all three; A1 A = 2/5, B = -4/5, C = -1.
parts.er: Well known; substitution (x = 2, -1/2, 0) most reliable; comparing coefficients more error-prone; few multiplied by (2x + 1)^3 (ER pp.3-4).

parts.ask: Hence exact value of the integral from 7 to 12 of (3x + 4)/((x - 2)(2x + 1)^2) dx.
parts.final_form: p ln q + r, rational p, q, r
parts.ms: M1 ln forms for the linear terms; M1 k/(2x + 1)^2 -> K/(2x + 1); A1ft (2/5) ln(x - 2) - (2/5) ln(2x + 1) + 1/(4x + 2); dM1 limits; M1 log laws to combine; A1 (2/5) ln(6/5) - 1/75 oe.
parts.er: Most scored 3 method marks; the 1/2 in the integral of 1/(2x + 1) was often missed; (2x + 1)^-2 integrated with sign/coefficient errors or as a ln; messy single logs; combining logs before substituting was more successful (ER pp.3-4).

parts.ask: Curve y^2 x + 3y = 4x^2 + k, y > 0: dy/dx in terms of x and y.
parts.ms: M1 implicit differentiation of y^2 x or 3y; A1 y^2 x -> 2xy dy/dx + y^2; A1 3 dy/dx and 8x; dM1 collect; A1 dy/dx = (8x - y^2)/(2xy + 3).
parts.er: Well done; errors in the product rule on y^2 x (one term, or three dy/dx terms); +k sometimes differentiated into the answer (ER pp.4-5).

parts.ask: P(p, 2) is the minimum turning point of C: (i) p; (ii) k.
parts.ms: M1 dy/dx = 0 with y = 2 gives 8x - 4 = 0; A1 p = 1/2; M1 substitute into C; A1 k = 7. Alt: quadratic in p with a repeated root (discriminant zero).
parts.er: Generally known; p = 2 (from 8p = 4) a common slip; those with k in the derivative struggled; few used the discriminant route (ER pp.4-5).

parts.ask: Cone, fixed height 5 cm, base radius r, slant height l: l in terms of r.
parts.ms: B1 l = sqrt(25 + r^2).
parts.er: Errors: l^2 = 25 - r^2, answer left as l^2, and l = r + 5 (ER pp.5-6).

parts.ask: Radius increasing at 3 cm per minute; S = pi r^2 + pi r l: rate of change of S when r = 1.5 cm.
parts.ms: M1A1 dS/dr of pi r^2 + pi r sqrt(25 + r^2) (product and chain rules); M1 dS/dt = (dS/dr) x 3 at r = 1.5; A1 81.5.
parts.er: Challenging for most: connected rates poorly understood; many treated l as a constant instead of using (a); product-rule errors; most scored only the chain-rule method mark (ER pp.5-6).

parts.ask: The integral of x^2 cos 2x dx.
parts.ms: M1A1 first parts: (1/2)x^2 sin 2x - integral of x sin 2x dx; M1 parts again; A1 (1/2)x^2 sin 2x + (1/2)x cos 2x - (1/4) sin 2x + c.
parts.er: Well drilled; errors were mainly sign slips in the second application, often when the stages were done separately and combined (ER p.6).

parts.ask: dy/dt = (t cos t/y)^2: solve, giving y^n = f(t).
parts.ms: B1 separate: integral of y^2 dy = integral of t^2 cos^2 t dt; M1 y^3/3; M1 cos^2 t = (1 + cos 2t)/2; M1 use (a); A1ft y^3 = (1/2)t^3 + (3/4)t^2 sin 2t + (3/4)t cos 2t - (3/8) sin 2t + c.
parts.er: Separation usually good (y^-2 errors); many used the double angle identity and (a), but some restarted parts or integrated cos^2 t wrongly; '+c' often missing, losing the final mark (ER p.6).

parts.ask: l1: r = 3i + pj + 7k + lambda(2i - 5j + 4k); l2: r = 8i - 2j + 5k + mu(4i + j + 2k) intersect: find p.
parts.ms: M1 equate components; M1 solve two equations (mu = -2, lambda = -3/2); M1 third equation for p; A1 p = -23/2.
parts.er: Well answered; some long circuitous substitution routes with fractions caused errors (ER pp.7-8).

parts.ask: Position vector of the point of intersection.
parts.ms: M1 substitute mu; A1 -4j + k.
parts.er: Mostly correct via l2; using l1 relied on earlier values; some left blank (ER pp.7-8).

parts.ask: Acute angle between l1 and l2.
parts.er: Scalar product well known; errors: position vectors used instead of directions, 2 s.f. answer, obtuse angle (ER pp.7-8).

parts.ask: A on l1 with lambda = 2; B on l2 with AB perpendicular to l2: coordinates of B.
parts.ms: B1ft OA = 7i - (43/2)j + 15k; M1 AB in terms of mu; M1 AB.(4i + j + 2k) = 0 so mu = -1/6; dM1 substitute into l2; A1 (22/3, -13/6, 14/3).
parts.er: Discriminating; OA usually found, often the only mark; OB rather than AB dotted with the direction; sign errors in mu (ER pp.7-8).

parts.ask: Using u = 4x + 2 sin 2x (or otherwise): integral from 0 to pi/2 of e^(4x + 2 sin 2x) cos^2 x dx = (1/8)(e^(2pi) - 1).
parts.ms: M1A1 du/dx = 4 + 4 cos 2x; M1 = 8 cos^2 x so the integral becomes integral of e^u/8 du; A1ft (1/8)e^u with limits 0 and 2pi; A1* cso. Alternative by inspection.
parts.er: Many lost the final marks by jumping to the given answer without the integral in u and its limits; double angle use often not shown; 'show that' needs every step (ER pp.8-9).

parts.ask: y = 6e^(2x + sin 2x) cos x; R (positive axes and the curve up to x = pi/2) rotated 2pi about the x-axis: volume using (a).
parts.ms: B1 V = pi integral of y^2 dx = 36pi integral of e^(4x + 2 sin 2x) cos^2 x dx; M1 use (a); A1 (9pi/2)(e^(2pi) - 1).
parts.er: Many wrote pi integral of y^2 but could not square y or link to (a); those who did rarely lost pi (ER pp.8-9).

parts.ask: Proof by contradiction: y = 2x + x^3 + cos x has no stationary points.
parts.ms: B1 assume dy/dx = 0 for some x; M1 dy/dx = 2 + 3x^2 - sin x; dM1 sin x = 3x^2 + 2 >= 2; A1cso contradiction since |sin x| <= 1, so no stationary points.
parts.er: Set-up and differentiation usually fine; many then just asserted no solutions without a reason (needs sin x <= 1 and 3x^2 + 2 >= 2); graphs alone, discriminants or testing values scored nothing further; conclusion must mention both contradiction and no stationary points (ER p.9).

parts.ask: x = sec t, y = sqrt3 tan(t + pi/3), pi/6 < t < pi/2: dy/dx in terms of t.
parts.ms: B1 dx/dt = sec t tan t and dy/dt = sqrt3 sec^2(t + pi/3); M1A1 dy/dx = sqrt3 sec^2(t + pi/3)/(sec t tan t).
parts.er: sec t usually differentiated correctly; quotient-rule routes rarely worked; 'cancelling' sec with different arguments was a common error (ER pp.9-12).

parts.ask: Tangent at t = pi/3.
parts.ms: B1 (2, -3); M1 gradient 2; M1A1 cso y = 2x - 7.
parts.er: Tackled well; some found the normal, some did not evaluate the gradient numerically (ER pp.9-12).

parts.ask: All points satisfy y = (Ax^2 + B sqrt(3x^2 - 3))/(4 - 3x^2); find A, B.
parts.final_form: given form with A and B
parts.ms: M1 compound angle tan(t + pi/3); M1A1 tan t = sqrt(x^2 - 1) from sec^2 = 1 + tan^2; M1 rationalise the denominator; A1 (3x^2 + 4 sqrt(3x^2 - 3))/(4 - 3x^2).
parts.er: Challenging finish; most expanded tan(t + pi/3) and used sec^2 = 1 + tan^2, but rationalising to the required form defeated all but the most able; finding A and B from points without justifying the form scored nothing (ER pp.9-12).

parts.ask: (No calculator-only solutions.) Proof by contradiction that y = 8 + 8x - (15/2)x^2 does not meet y = A - 8x + x^2/2 + Bx^3 for 0 < x < 8/3.
parts.ms: M1 assume they meet and equate; M1 rearrange to 0 = 8(x^2 - 2x) + 8 + x^3/24, i.e. complete the square; A1 0 = 8(x - 1)^2 + x^3/24; A1 argue 8(x - 1)^2 >= 0 and x^3/24 > 0 for 0 < x < 8/3, so the sum is positive: contradiction, with a conclusion.
